problem_type: customCall HTTP transport decoded every upstream response as UTF-8/JSON and serialized sandbox host values solely through JSON strings, corrupting binary media responses and breaking saveFile(bytes)
symptom: When an upstream endpoint returned raw binary bytes (e.g. video/mp4, audio/mpeg, or application/octet-stream containing non-UTF-8 sequences), http.get / http.post / request handed the QuickJS script a UTF-8 replacement-corrupted string, causing saveFile(bytes, 'mp4') to throw 'TypeError: saveFile bytes 必须是 ArrayBuffer、Uint8Array 或数字数组' or write corrupted bytes.
direct_cause: customCallRunner.doRequest unconditionally called requestJson / requestMultipart (responseKind='json' -> bytes.toString('utf8')), and customCallSandbox passed all host-to-guest values via JSON.stringify / context.newString and guest-to-host saveFile payloads via JSON number arrays.
class_root: Assuming every HTTP response in a general-purpose user script boundary is UTF-8 JSON instead of honoring RFC 9110 Content-Type framing at the transport decoder and transferring binary buffers natively across the QuickJS FFI boundary.
affected_population: All custom-call scripts calling http.get, http.post, or request against synchronous binary endpoints (video download streams, TTS audio streams, multipart image/video endpoints) and saving output via saveFile(bytes, ext, contentType)

external_sources.purpose: Defines media-type framing for distinguishing structured JSON/textual representations from binary representations.
Binary HTTP bodies must be consumed as raw byte buffers (ArrayBuffer / Uint8Array) rather than UTF-8 text.

invariants: customCall HTTP requests route through requestBinary (supporting JSON, string, and FormData bodies) so non-JSON, non-text responses are never passed through bytes.toString('utf8') while HTTP errors and HTTP 200 JSON logical-error envelopes still throw VendorRequestError.

decodeCustomCallHttpResponse is the single decoder translating BinaryVendorResponse into parsed JSON (for application/json and +json), UTF-8 text / JSON (for textual media types), or raw Buffer (for binary media types and non-UTF-8 unlabeled payloads).

Binary buffers cross Host <-> QuickJS via native context.newArrayBuffer and context.getArrayBuffer so guest scripts receive genuine Uint8Array instances and saveFile transfers raw bytes without JSON array memory blowup.

door_reduction.why_not: customCallDispatch and customCallIpc already converge on runCustomCallScript, which now uses a single requestBinary transport call instead of branching between requestMultipart and requestJson.

generality_proof: Routing every customCall HTTP call (GET, JSON POST, raw body, and FormData multipart) through requestBinary -> decodeCustomCallHttpResponse -> QuickJS ArrayBuffer FFI preserves exact byte identity for any binary media type (video/*, audio/*, image/*, application/octet-stream) while keeping JSON and text scripts 100% compatible.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single owner decoding customCall HTTP responses by Content-Type into parsed JSON, UTF-8 text, or raw binary bytes.
Single script execution entry wiring vendorHttp.requestBinary, transcript redaction/preview, and saveFile.
Single QuickJS realm bridge marshaling binary payloads via native ArrayBuffer handles in both directions.
Shared byte-preserving vendor HTTP executor supporting JSON, string, and FormData bodies with unified auth, timeout, and logical-error envelope checks.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Production runTask custom-call execution delegates to runCustomCallScript.
Onboarding trial run IPC delegates to runCustomCallScript.

recurrence.reason: Prior tests constructed Uint8Array inside the script or wrapped byte arrays in application/json ({ bytes: [...] }), masking the transport and FFI UTF-8/JSON bottlenecks across all binary customCall endpoints.

prevention.invariant: Binary HTTP responses arrive in QuickJS as Uint8Array backed by native ArrayBuffer and saveFile validates ArrayBuffer / ArrayBufferView / byte array inputs before passing raw bytes to writeGeneratedAsset.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid saveFile inputs throw TypeError inside the sandbox; corrupted or non-matching media bytes fail writeGeneratedAsset magic-byte validation (NOMI_ERR::output-unreadable).
prevention.strategy: Decode HTTP responses once in decodeCustomCallHttpResponse by Content-Type, marshal binary buffers natively via QuickJS newArrayBuffer/getArrayBuffer, and test real non-UTF-8 binary HTTP responses end-to-end.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed the JSON-only requestMultipart/requestJson branch in customCallRunner.doRequest and the JSON number-array saveFile bridge in customCallSandbox in the same commit.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Uses quickjs-emscripten@0.32.0 native newArrayBuffer and getArrayBuffer APIs already installed in the repository; no dependency version or lifecycle change.

migration: Existing JSON customCall scripts (including { bytes: [...] } JSON envelopes) and text scripts continue to receive parsed JSON or strings; binary Content-Type responses now return Uint8Array directly matching customCallContract.ts.
residual_risks: QuickJS sandbox memory limit remains 64 MiB, bounding single in-sandbox binary buffers to under ~50 MiB.
